sections.heading: What is Discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness?

blocks.text: **Discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness** is a compile-time TypeScript concept that erases at emit — the run-time behavior is still JavaScript. Discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness lets TypeScript narrow unions after runtime checks — typeof, in, instanceof, user-defined predicates, and assert functions. This section defines terms before code — read the glossary, then run the snippets in Node or the browser console.

sections.heading: Why Discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness matters in production

blocks.text: Senior interviews and on-call debugging both test **Discriminated unions and switch exhaustiveness** beyond one-line definitions. Production failures here look like silent data corruption, memory growth, type errors at CI, or async ordering bugs — not syntax errors. If you know JavaScript, use the comparison table to transfer intuition instead of memorizing rules in isolation.
